newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: UK'S CROWN AGENTS TAKES OVER MOZAMBIQUE CUSTOMS.
newsitem.headline: UK'S CROWN AGENTS TAKES OVER MOZAMBIQUE CUSTOMS.

text.p: The Mozambican government will hand over the management of its customs service to a British firm on Friday next week, the company announced on Thursday.
Crown Agents, a British consultancy, has been appointed by the government in Maputo to run customs until the year 2000, the new manager, Chris Outhwaite, told a news conference.
The company's immediate objective is to crack down on rampant smuggling, especially from neighbouring South Africa.
Outhwaite, former chief internal auditor of British customs, said anti-smuggling teams would be mobilised without delay.
"The project in Mozambique is unique in its scope," he said.
"It is ambitious and shows great courage on the part of the government of Mozambique in placing its trust in a team of British customs officers."

Outhwaite said Crown Agents intended to: "Prevent the present huge loss of revenue, to take punitive action against offenders against customs laws and to improve the reputation of customs -- not least by taking stern action against corruption and other malpractise".
Pedro Bule, director of the government's customs restructuring unit, told the same news conference that Mozambique had given Crown Agents a wide scope.

"The aim...is to promote complete administrative reorganisation, review and modernise all customs legislation, revise all operational proceedings and train operational and management staff," Bule said.

At present a bottle of smuggled Scotch whisky in a Maputo shop costs about half the price of the same bottle in a store in Scotland and smuggled South African cigarettes have brought the Mozambican tobacco industry close to ruin.
A Maputo cigarette company owner greeted the customs announcement with glee, telling Reuters: "It's time to celebrate. I have a bottle of champagne in the car!"
